parsed.attack: The briefing is built from 'what last year's notes said went wrong in the same week', which means season one has nothing to say - the subscriber pays $4 a month for roughly twelve months before the product becomes the thing that was sold to them, and they must spend that year logging sowings in the rain to make it so. Meanwhile every generic version of the weekly answer is already free and well loved by exactly this cohort: the RHS monthly job list, Gardeners' World, Charles Dowding's channel, the association newsletter and the person on the next plot, who also knows your soil. The price is the tell - UK allotment rents run roughly £40-70 a year, so a $48-a-year subscription costs about what the land costs, and this is a demographic that skews older, analogue and deliberately frugal; the plot exists partly because growing your own is cheaper. The evidence cited is three closures plus a reinterpretation of why they closed, with no allotment holder anywhere in it.
parsed.strongest_defence: Ten minutes of setup entering this season's bed plan makes the first briefing non-empty from week one, and the association channel is close to free distribution into a community that already organises around noticeboards and newsletters; at £3 a month against a plot people spend hundreds of hours on, price is not the objection - forgetting what you did last April is.
parsed.verdict_reason: The personalised value the pitch rests on requires a year of user-supplied logging before it exists, while the generic version of the same briefing is already free and habitual for this audience.
